description:
## Why this issue exists

`TypeFilter::allows()` in kithd/src/events.rs handles three known JMAP type name strings. For any other name it returns `false` and fires a `debug_assert!(false)` that only fires in debug builds. In release builds an unrecognized type name is silently dropped — the SSE push is never delivered for that type.

If a developer adds a new JMAP broadcast type (e.g. `Email/changes`) but forgets to extend the `TypeFilter` match arm, the feature will appear to work in `cargo test` (debug build with assertions) but SSE subscribers that filter on that type will silently receive nothing in production.

## What needs to be done

Replace the `debug_assert!(false)` / silent-false fallthrough with one of:
- A hard match that is `unreachable!()` (or a named error) so the compiler forces callers to handle it
- A simple `Default::default()` + log at WARN level so production telemetry catches the gap
- Document the closed set of type names as a compile-time enum so the match is exhaustive

At minimum, add a `tracing::warn!` call in the unknown-name branch so the problem is observable in production logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Adding a new broadcast type without updating `TypeFilter` causes a compile error (preferred) or a visible log warning in release builds
- No silent event loss for unrecognized type names
title: TypeFilter::allows silently drops unknown type names in release builds
